hypotheses.statement: The original disease-defining report for PARK27 is the 2025 preprint/2026 journal article by Magrinelli et al., which first links biallelic PSMF1 variants to early-onset Parkinson disease/parkinsonism in patients.
hypotheses.rationale: PubMed searches return this paper as the earliest direct PSMF1-parkinsonism match; if an older report exists, it should appear in the citation graph or under alternate gene/protein names such as PI31.

hypotheses.statement: A small number of later papers extend the patient spectrum of PARK27 rather than redefining the disorder, including cohort/letter reports such as the 2026 German Parkinson's disease cohort paper.
hypotheses.rationale: Rare Mendelian PD genes commonly accrue follow-up cohort screens and short communications after the first report; these should contain additional variant carriers or negative cohort screening and can be distinguished from the original report by publication type and date.

hypotheses.statement: Functional studies on PARK27 will center on proteasome regulation and mitochondrial dysfunction, using patient fibroblasts and animal models to show that disease variants impair PI31/PSMF1 activity and cellular energetics.
hypotheses.rationale: The 2026 Nature Communications article already indexes fibroblasts, mice, and Drosophila in MeSH terms, indicating mechanistic validation beyond patient ascertainment; these experiments are likely the main functional literature for the disease variants.

You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

system:
You maintain the map of an investigation: hypothesis regions (kinds of answer) and observation regions (kinds of evidence), each grouped under axes. A map holds at most 10 regions per space, and the observation map is full. Before this round explores, decide which regions to fold into one, so there is room for at least one new region in each full space.

## How to merge

- Merge regions that have turned out to mean the same thing, or that differ on a distinction the evidence has not needed.
- Merge regions that went nowhere -- UNTRIED, or every hypothesis in them shelved -- into the nearest live region, so the map keeps what the search has learned and drops what it has not used.
- Do not merge two regions that still hold competing live hypotheses: the point of the map is to keep them apart.
- Each merge names two or more existing regions, the merged region's name (new, or one of the members), its axis, what it covers, and why. A merged region keeps every hypothesis and observation of its members.
- At least one merge per full space. Several are fine. Call submit_merges once.

system:
You open lines of investigation. You map where answers and evidence could lie, and propose hypotheses to test. Others build and test them; you do not judge them.

## The map

- Hypothesis regions: kinds of answer, grouped under axes (the dimensions answers differ along).
- Observation regions: kinds of evidence, grouped under axes (where and how one would look).
- Add a region only if it is distinct from every region already on the map. Add an axis only if it is new, or subsumes an existing axis (then set `replaces_axis`).
- Each map holds at most 10 regions. A region proposed to a full map is dropped, and a hypothesis naming a region that is not on the map is left unplaced; file it in an existing region instead.
- You can use the tools to look at the environment before you propose; a hypothesis grounded in what exists beats one about what might.

## Hypotheses

- Propose 3 hypotheses in the least explored regions and axes (counts are shown; UNTRIED regions and thin axes first). Each needs a testable `statement`, a `rationale`, and a `region`.
- Make them compete: different regions, different mechanisms, not variants of one idea.
- Read the evidence on last round's hypotheses and every hypothesis's metrics per part of the task. Do not re-propose what is held.
- If hypotheses win on different parts, or the best score has stopped improving, at least one proposal must be a combination (name the hypotheses and what it takes from each).
- Call submit_exploration once.

system:
You decide what happens to each tested hypothesis next, from the evidence.

## Decisions

- `keep`: the claim stands as it is; it is carried forward without retesting.
- `refine`: the claim needs a changed clause, scope or mechanism; give the new `statement`. It is tested as a new hypothesis.
- `shelve`: set it aside. It can be revived later if the run stops making progress.

## How to decide

- A result that rests on one measurement of one artifact is weak evidence either way.
- Do not shelve a claim that wins on some part of the task, even if it loses overall: say so in `rationale`.
- Weigh what supports each claim against what refutes it, and cite those observation ids in `rationale`.
- Decide every hypothesis listed. Call submit_revision once.

h_regions.name: Primary disease-defining report
h_regions.description: Papers that first establish PSMF1 as a cause of autosomal recessive early-onset Parkinson disease / parkinsonism in affected patients, including the original family or families.

h_regions.name: Subsequent patient series
h_regions.description: Later case reports, cohort screens, letters, or replications reporting additional affected individuals or cohorts with PSMF1 variants and similar phenotypes.

h_regions.name: Functional mechanism study
h_regions.description: Experimental papers testing disease-associated PSMF1 variants or PI31 function in cells or model organisms, including proteasome, mitochondrial, and neurodegeneration assays.

h_regions.name: Preprint-to-journal transition
h_regions.description: The disease-defining PSMF1 report first appeared as a preprint and was later formalized as the journal article; the key question is whether the preprint or journal version should be treated as the primary defining publication.

h_regions.name: Single-family founder report
h_regions.description: The PARK27 literature may be anchored in one extended family or kindred with a shared biallelic PSMF1 founder variant, with later papers mainly adding relatives or phenotype details rather than independent families.

h_regions.name: Loss-of-function allelic spectrum
h_regions.description: Disease-causing PARK27 variants may include truncating, splice, or other loss-of-function alleles that correlate with more severe or earlier-onset disease, including perinatal lethality, rather than only missense changes.

h_regions.name: Cross-gene mechanistic precursor
h_regions.description: Papers on PI31/PSMF1 biology, proteasome regulation, or related parkinsonism models that predate PARK27 but are not themselves patient-defining PSMF1 disease reports; these may later be cited as mechanistic context.

h_regions.name: Conference-to-publication bridge
h_regions.description: A preprint, abstract, or conference-like record that is not yet the definitive journal article but may contain the earliest public disease description or variant data for PSMF1/PARK27.

h_regions.name: Independent second family
h_regions.description: A separate, unrelated patient pedigree or cohort with biallelic PSMF1 variants and similar phenotype that is distinct from the original core family/pedigree and not merely a follow-up screen or reanalysis.

h_regions.name: Negative cohort screening
h_regions.description: Papers that explicitly report screening a Parkinson disease cohort for PSMF1 variants and finding none, or only rare findings without establishing a new family, serving as negative or low-yield follow-up evidence.

o_regions.name: PubMed query with gene-disease synonyms
o_regions.description: Searches combining PSMF1, PI31/proteasome regulator synonyms, Parkinson disease/parkinsonism, and early-onset/recessive terms to capture papers using older or alternate nomenclature.

o_regions.name: Primary disease-defining report
o_regions.description: Search and metadata evidence used to find the PSMF1/PARK27 literature, including publication-type distinctions and synonym-based retrieval.
